So I never engaged in working meetings at receptions of this kind and therefore I could not engage in them with you. Now, did you, or how did you receive invitations to attend those receptions within the Novo Demokracija party's quota? You say you weren't a member of the leadership. You say you were an advisor to the president. So how were you invited to those receptions?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, but these are three questions at once, if I understand this correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just answer the last one: How were you invited to the receptions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was invited in writing within the quota of Novo Demokracija, and I never said that I was never an official of Novo Demokracija. I was first and foremost an advisor there, but I also carried out other duties, and I got invitations regularly and they do exist in the register.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. In the quota of Novo Demokracija.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I really am not involved in quotas here. I'm not dealing in quotas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, there may be a temptation to argue with the accused. Would you resist it. Just remember, you're in a court, answering questions, and don't personalise it. Mr. Milosevic, on your side, would you slow down when you're asking questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: My next question is quite brief. Did you represent yourself falsely here? I mean your capacity, not your name and surname, the capacity that you had. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Allow me to read something to you, and then I'm going to ask you for an answer to this question. This is what Novo Demokracija, that is to say, your party, stated yesterday, after your statement here: Novo Demokracija stated the following, your party. As you mentioned, its president is the current Minister of the Interior, that is to say, my political opponent, at any rate. So this is what it says: "The content of the testimony of Ratomir Tanic testifies to his attempt to construct a story in which Novo Demokracija did not take part in the way in which he has presented this, nor did he have the importance that he wishes to attach to himself. According to our knowledge, Tanic least of all could have been a partner to Milosevic in carrying out some kind of plan in order to restore to Kosovo its autonomy."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you get interpretation of this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, but we're going to stop anyway. Mr. Milosevic, what are you reading from?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This morning's paper. I'll give it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just finish. Belgrade morning newspapers that I got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. No. Unless there's a specific question, this is all comment by somebody else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a specific question. Please. This is not a comment. This is an official statement of his party, and in relation to this official statement, I wish to put a question to him, and I'm trying to read it. It's very short. "'Imagination does all sorts of things, and necessity even more, and we have understanding for the Tanic case,' was stated yesterday by Novo Demokracija."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm not going to permit this. This is pure comment by a journalist or somebody putting out a statement. Now, if you've got a question, you can ask the witness a question rather than reading out this kind of thing from newspapers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to read this to you. This is a statement of his party, a press release. It is not interpretation by journalists

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment. I'll consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, who wrote this article?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not an article. I told you: This is a press release issued by his party. This was issued by his own party. That's why I'm asking him about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It doesn't matter for a moment. Which journalist reported it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this photocopy that I got by fax, there is no signature of any journalist. This is a daily newspaper called Blic, today's newspaper. A journal of this nature --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. It doesn't matter. I just wanted to understand the position. Now, what we're not going to permit is a lot of abuse, if that is coming. What you can ask the witness about is questions which go to his credibility. Comments like "imagination" and the rest of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it are of no assistance to us at all and we're not going to allow questions about that. Now, is there something concrete in that that you want to put to the witness? For instance, that his representation of his position is incorrect. Now, if that appears, then you can ask it. But merely to read out a lot of comment about his evidence from whoever is not going to assist. Now, can you find a concrete question to arise from it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am putting the question on the basis of a very brief sentence that is part of the press release issued by his party and which reads as follows: "Therefore, we are unaware of his decision to testify about something that we do not know that he took part in." That's it. Could it be more specific than that? His party does not know about his participation in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, that is the question. Now, Mr. Tanic, what he's put to you is that your party do not know about your decision to testify, and it's --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And it's something that we do not know that he took part in. It's not at all clear what that means, but we'll allow you to reply.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I shall give a very simple answer. A party with a membership of 35.000 or 40.000 members cannot know everything that its top leadership does. That is one point. The second point is that many things that I presented here today are things that were unknown to the public of Serbia. Until now these were secret matters, as far as many politicians were concerned, as far as, unfortunately, many members of my party were concerned as well, because Mr. Milosevic concealed these facts so they really do not know about everything that I took part in. That is true. As a party, they do not know about everything that I took part in but therefore, the Ministry of the Interior, Mr. Dusan Mihajlovic, knows that full well and he knows that for two and a half years I have not been in the country and I never said that in this courtroom I represent Novo Demokracija. I said that I am a private person here, that after torture and after kidnapping, I have been an exiled person, so for two and a half years they haven't known whether I've been dead or alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The question did not relate to your current status, that I also have my doubts, but their claim - and this is not a membership of 30.000, this is your party - that you are talking about something that they are not aware of your participation in, and you claim that you did participate in this. Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me who signed this press release? I never said that I participated in this through them. This was in the president's office, Mr. Mihajlovic's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who was the president of the party?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Both slow down for the record. Now, the witness, I think, has dealt with the question of whether the party knew or not. Have you got another question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just ask him one more thing. How does he react to the fact that some persons that he mentioned yesterday in relation to the talks that he allegedly had with them sent letters this morning that they are challenging everything he said in its entirety? I have a letter of Ratko Markovic stating that he had no talks with him before going to Rambouillet, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can call Mr. Markovic. You can call him to give evidence and deny it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I answer this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, you can answer about Mr. Markovic, but shortly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I didn't put a question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My talks, my work, can be shown and proven through independent statements from at least three sides. Mr. Milosevic can seek these statements, and of course people now are going to deny, after this was said, that they had ever met me, because they will be afraid to go through the same things that I went through, an attempt of assassination, et cetera. I can always prove all my contacts from at least two or three independent sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you accusing me of some kind of an assassination attempt?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't reply to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Since you won't let me show these other letters, I will go on, but please save my time and do not interject. What are you by profession?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a political emigre now, but before that, I was a businessman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what kind of an education do you have? What did you train for?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I graduated from elementary school and I am literate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to answer questions of this nature, because I already had them put to me in a basement while I was tortured by your men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who tortured you because you say yourself that these were people who were against me. I'm not going to go into all of that now. Now I'm putting a very legitimate question to you, because I'm trying to establish your credibility. What kind of education do you have? That is no secret.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I studied economics and philosophy, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you graduate?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That really is not for this Court to deal with, or is it for me to deal with. I don't really think I have to answer this kind of question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, is there any reason why you can't tell us that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I do not wish to do that, because I was not an expert witness here in order to have my education established. I said very precisely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: These are some very basic questions. It seems to me there's no prejudice to you in answering them. Now, is there any reason at all why you can't tell us if you graduated or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, of course there is a reason, because why would I answer personal questions? The next question, then, is going to be my sock size. I didn't ask Mr. Milosevic what kind of school he graduated from, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, you will answer proper questions and you will answer properly. That was a perfectly proper question. There's no reason the Court can see why you shouldn't answer. If you choose not to, the fact that you don't will be noted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I studied economics and philosophy, and as for the question where I graduated from and what kind of a degree I have, that is a question that I am unwilling to answer, and I hope I have the right to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, are you an ungraduated student of philosophy and economics; one who has not graduated?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that can be -- from my previous question, I said that I did not want to answer that question, and I don't want to answer it in any other way. I said nothing here to do with a diploma linked to the faculty of philosophy or economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right, so what you're saying is your education level is a secondary education level; is that it? A gymnasium.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not complete a gymnasium, a secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What school do you have, then?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secondary economics school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, so secondary economics, school of economics; is that it?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said. We would have to call in experts here to ascertain the level of education, and I don't wish to answer questions that have nothing to do with this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But they do have to do with this trial, because I'm trying to establish your credibility, and of course your answers here do that for me. Now, where were you employed and where did you receive a salary during the time you say you were performing all these tasks, doing all this work that you claim you were doing? During that time, where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a salary and therefore was employed in my own enterprise, my own company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where did you say? Where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my own company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, your own company.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had three companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Your present job, does it entail the duty to give out insider explanations to this false accusation that has been raised here, false indictment?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am not duty-bound with respect to this trial at all or with respect to any insider explanations or any other political obligations with anything that is false or true, nor do I know that this is a false indictment, as you have termed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you understand that it is very easy to see how parts of the indictment coincide with the pamphlet you wrote on 30 pages, that you wrote in the form of your statement? Do you realise that?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there is a coincidence, then probably coincidence of fact. I did not write the indictment, and I doubt that I am qualified to write it. We talked about that a moment ago. So quite certainly I did not study law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know it is a generally known fact that the indictment was compiled in cooperation with the British service which you worked for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Totally irrelevant. Not for the witness to deal with. Next question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And is this fact relevant: The fact that Mr. Nice presented, which was that when the statements of this witness were made, that there were two members of the British intelligence service present. Is that a relevant fact?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me or are you asking the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is a matter you can ask about, yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, if you did not take part and cooperate in writing the indictment, why, then, would they change your identity and ensure a new country for you to reside in and spend enormous money on your protection programme, when you are allegedly testifying here to some generally known political matters?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not testifying here on general political matters but very specific secrets which your regime tried to hush up, and they are providing protection for me, I assume, because with all their check-outs that they have done, they have established that I was at least the victim of torture, perhaps even an attempted murder, together with my wife, and people from the British intelligence service was there as security and not to tell me what to do or what to write. Because they did not know about many of the things that you did, so how could they tell me what to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many people from the British intelligence service were present while you were making your statement?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know whether they were people from the British service or from the British Security Service. There's a vast difference between the two. For brief periods of time, one person would be present for physical protection, and he was never present throughout nor did he influence the proceedings and statement in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to answer my questions. Your opinions and your explanations are something else.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those are facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not interested in them. Now, are you clear on the following: Do you know at least that in writing the indictment, the same individuals participated from Serbia who throughout all these years were the internal fulcrum for the media war against Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The writing of the indictment is nothing to do with this witness. It's a matter for the Prosecution. So there's no point asking him questions about it. Now, have you got another question for him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, don't you think that, in fact, it is precisely by what you have written in your statement and through your oral testimony that in a way you have in fact confirmed that you are -- were one of the associates, in a way, in the writing of the indictment? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Not for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it clear to you that you are appearing here in that so-called role of an insider, the role of an insider which you in fact did not have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a matter of comment too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you understand that every literate citizen of Serbia can compare that, what you're saying here and what it says in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you are wasting your time and the time of the Court with these comments. Now, there are two minutes left. You can ask another question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd like to move on to the point that was made about ethnic cleansing, but as you tell me that I have only two minutes left, then it would be senseless to go into that now, to move on to that area now. So let me ask one interim question, if I can put it that way, a brief one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Why did you seek the status of a secret witness?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not seek for that, nor was it the status of a secret witness. I'm here with my name and surname, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, come on.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I be a secret witness if I have a name and a surname?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Just a moment. Just a moment. There's too much interruption going on. Right. You've got one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact - let me rephrase my question - that until the day before yesterday, until the end of business the day before yesterday, you were before this illegal institution as a secret witness under the term K3, the code term K3?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, Mr. Milosevic, is something I neither knew nor sought to know. And as I am testifying here under my own name and surname, I don't know that, and I'm here under my own name and not under some secret name. And you can sully the name as much as you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're going to adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, if you want us to have the witness statement at any time, the statement of this witness, perhaps you could let the Court know and we'll have copies of them so we can read it over the adjournment, if there's some point you want to make on the statement. You can think about that. We'll adjourn now. 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th day of May, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
